theme: The eight visions begin; the Branch foretold
readingInstruction: Read Zechariah 1:1-3:10. Zechariah begins with a call to return, and then he sees eight night visions. Today you will read the first four. Read for what each one says about God’s care for Jerusalem and his people.
settingTheScene: Zechariah began prophesying two months after Haggai. He was both a prophet and a priest. His book is full of visions, symbols, and messianic promises, and it is the longest of the Minor Prophets. The first six chapters report eight visions that came in one night. They reassure the discouraged community that God has not forgotten Jerusalem.
observation: “Return to me, says the LORD of hosts, and I will return to you” (1:3).
“Your fathers, where are they? And the prophets, do they live forever? But my words and my statutes… did they not overtake your fathers?” (1:5-6).
“I have returned to Jerusalem with mercy; my house shall be built in it” (1:16).
“Jerusalem shall be inhabited as villages without walls, because of the multitude of people and livestock in it” (2:4).
“And I will be to her a wall of fire all around, declares the LORD, and I will be the glory in her midst” (2:5).
“Sing and rejoice, O daughter of Zion, for behold, I come and I will dwell in your midst” (2:10).
“Is not this a brand plucked from the fire?” (3:2).
“Behold, I have taken your iniquity away from you, and I will clothe you with pure vestments” (3:4).
interpretation:
The book opens with a call that matches the whole Old Testament: “Return to me, and I will return to you.” The previous generation did not listen, but God’s word did what it said. “They repented and said, As the LORD of hosts purposed to deal with us… so has he dealt with us.” Now it is the new generation’s turn.

The visions follow. The first is a man on a red horse among myrtle trees, with angelic patrols. They report that the earth is at rest. But the angel asks, “O LORD of hosts, how long?” The LORD answers with “gracious and comforting words”: “I am exceedingly jealous for Jerusalem.” The second vision, four horns and four craftsmen, shows that the powers that scattered Judah will be dealt with.

The third vision is a man with a measuring line, ready to measure Jerusalem. An angel says that the city will be unwalled, because there will be so many people. And God himself will be “a wall of fire all around” and “the glory in her midst.” This is better than any stone wall. It was wonderful news for those who were proud of Nehemiah’s wall: the true security was the presence of God. “Many nations shall join themselves to the LORD in that day, and shall be my people.”

The fourth vision, in chapter 3, is the center. Joshua the high priest stands before the angel of the LORD, in filthy garments, with Satan at his right hand to accuse him. The LORD rebukes Satan: “Is not this a brand plucked from the fire?” Joshua’s filthy clothes are removed. “Behold, I have taken your iniquity away from you, and I will clothe you with pure vestments.” A clean turban is put on his head. The picture is of justification by grace. Joshua does nothing to earn it. The chapter ends with a promise of “my servant the Branch,” the coming Messiah, and “I will remove the iniquity of this land in a single day.”
connection: Romans 8:33-34: “Who shall bring any charge against God’s elect? It is God who justifies.” 2 Corinthians 5:21: for our sake he made him to be sin, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God. Revelation 7:14: they washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb. Isaiah 61:10: he has clothed me with the garments of salvation. Hebrews 10:10-14: one offering has perfected for all time. Revelation 12:10 describes the accuser of our brothers.
application:
When the accuser reminds you of your failures, answer with chapter 3: “The LORD rebuke you.” Remember you are a brand plucked from the fire.

Thank God for the clean clothes of Christ’s righteousness.

Remember that the best security is God’s presence, not any wall you have built.
prayerPrompts: Return to God, and thank him for returning to you.
Ask him to be a wall of fire around his people.
